text:
amal: quick thread — we're revisiting per-AZ egress accounting for private VPC controlplane. current ask: can we avoid per-tenant NAT gateways while preserving accurate cost attribution?
ryan: short answer: yes but tradeoffs. central NATs are cheaper operationally but obscure per-tenant cost/egress visibility. per-az nat per-tenant is clearer but explodes ENI/route table + cost.
sophia: what about hybrid: per-az shared NAT pools with tagging + flow logs for attribution? less ENI churn, still billable.
mike: tagging+flow logs is plausible but delayed and not perfect for real-time dashboards. also cross-account peering and shared gw costs muddy billing if we tag only at flowlog level.
amal: agreed. need must-haves: 1) accurate per-tenant billing within 5% monthly, 2) failover to regional relay without cross-tenant leakage, 3) low ops burden.
harpreet: idea: reserve per-tenant egress ranges (SNAT IP pools) assigned per-AZ but implemented via shared NAT instances that map ranges -> tenant. that keeps IP-preservation and small SEPARATE allocation for accounting.
ryan: nice. Implementation concerns: ENI quotas when mapping many small IP pools, and iptables rules count on the NAT instance. we'd need a scalable mapping layer (XDP or AF_XDP) or eBPF to avoid iptables explosion.
sophia: also runway: adding eBPF path is medium-risk. alternative: use per-tenant ephemeral ENIs that we attach on demand and let AWS handle SNAT; teardown after idle. hits attach/detach API rate limits at scale.
mike: attach/detach scale is the killer. we measured ~30 attaches/sec before soft limits requiring support. bursts during onboarding could throttle.
amal: can we combine: per-tenant IP ranges + shared NAT instances with eBPF-based DNAT/SNAT mapping + fallback to regional relay for cold tenants?
harpreet: yes. fallback semantics: prefer local per-AZ NAT mapping, if NAT pool exhausted or NAT instance unhealthy, route to regional relay that marks traffic with tenant tag in header for accounting and policy enforcement. ensure no return traffic leak.
ryan: important edge: cross-account peering — we can't inject tenant headers across peering. regional relay must live in same account or proxying mode. that has cost implications.
sophia: ops runbook question: how do we reconcile untagged egress (e.g., during fallback) in billing? propose a nightly job to correlate relay logs + flowlogs + request UUIDs to attribute residuals. resolution window 24h.
mike: sounds ok. alert if residual > 2% of tenant monthly egress.
amal: need small config snippet for router rules. pseudo:
```
# per-az route preference
10.0.0.0/16 -> local-nat (weight 100)
10.0.0.0/16 -> regional-relay (weight 10, blackhole on local-nat-health==false)
```
ryan: add health-check probe and iptables conntrack mirroring. when local-nat unhealthy, shift weight to relay. conntrack care to avoid half-open flows.
harpreet: also add quotas: per-tenant egress ip limit, burst allowance, and auto-escalation to dedicated NAT if consistently > X GB/day.
sophia: ops UI/console: show per-tenant egress by AZ, relay fallback counts, and orphaned/unattributed bytes. need a fast aggregate query (pre-aggregated by hour) to be practical.
amal: action items: 1) spike eBPF mapping prototype (harpreet + ryan), 2) simulation of attach/detach scale for ephemeral ENIs (mike), 3) sketch billing reconciliation flow (sophia). I'll run prioritization.
deploybot: deploy scheduled: arch/prototypes/egress-mapping-spike -> infra-ci tonight 02:30 UTC :rocket:
amal: thanks. one more Q — any compliance/regulatory blockers with labeling traffic at relay?
ryan: only if headers leak PII; we'll use tenant-id UUID and ensure TLS termination points respect regulation. no plaintext tenant metadata unless customer agreed.
amal: great. meeting if needed after spikes. :thumbsup:
